name: Elbow plank
movement: a straight-body hold on the forearms

phone.placement: Lay the phone on its side on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to where you will be.

words.hint: Phone on its side on the floor, side on to you, forearms down, whole body in frame.
words.start: Lay the phone on its side on the floor, then get into your plank, side on, down onto your forearms.
words.position: Side on to the phone, down on your forearms and toes, elbows under your shoulders, body in one line.
words.top: One straight line from shoulder to ankle, shoulders over the elbows.
howto: Forearms down, elbows under your shoulders, hands flat or lightly fisted.
Toes tucked, legs straight, one line from shoulder to ankle.
Squeeze the glutes and pull the ribs in so the hips neither sag nor pike.
Hold, breathing; drop the knees when the time is called.
words.cannot: The neck and head, and whether the shoulder blades are spread: it judges the shoulder over the elbow and the hip on the line, nothing above the shoulder.
words.about: Elbow plank — where your shoulder sits over your elbow, measured as the lean of your upper arm off vertical, allowed from 5° behind to 15° in front; and how far your hip sits off the straight line from shoulder to ankle, allowed ±5°. Above the line your hips are piked and are told to come down, below it they are sagging and are told to lift.
words.lost: Step into the camera, side on
words.safety: Drop to the knees rather than let the lower back sag. Stop if the lower back hurts.
words.easier: From the knees; a shorter hold.
words.harder: A longer hold; feet raised on a step.
words.mistakes: Hips sagging; hips piked up; shoulders drifting behind the elbows.

measurements.label: arm off vertical

settings.label: Shoulder in front of elbow, most

measurements.why: The upper arm's lean off vertical, positive toward the head. The shoulder belongs over the elbow or a little in front; behind it the joint takes the load at its weakest, so the band is not symmetric.

measurements.label: hip off the line
measurements.why: How far the hip sits off the shoulder-to-ankle line, as degrees of bend: positive piked up, negative sagging.

faults.label: Shoulders behind elbows
faults.text: Bring your shoulders over your elbows
faults.deep: Shoulders forward — they are well behind your elbows

faults.label: Shoulders ahead of elbows
faults.text: Bring your shoulders back over your elbows
faults.deep: Shoulders back — they are well ahead of your elbows

faults.label: Hips piked
faults.deep: Lower your hips — shoulders to heels in one line

faults.label: Hips sagging
faults.deep: Lift your hips — shoulders to heels in one line
